title: Cysteamine in association with standard therapy for the treatment of hospitalized patients with COVID-19 pneumonia: phase 2 study on safety of a new antiviral and direct therapy on the host
official: Cysteamine in association with standard therapy for the treatment of hospitalized patients with COVID-19 pneumonia: phase 2 study on safety of a new antiviral and direct therapy on the host
summary: Main objective: Safety of cysteamine in hospitalized patients with COVID-19 pneumonia not requiring high oxygen flows, whether or not previously vaccinated with anti-COVID-19 vaccines.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥18 years
2. Infertility condition (postmenopausal, surgically induced infertility e.g., vasectomy with documented azoospermia for men or tubal closure for women) or in potentially fertile subjects, negative urinary pregnancy test (women), and consent to adhere to the following contraception requirements from 2 weeks prior to enrollment to 18 weeks after experimental drug administration (men and women)
3. Positive nasopharyngeal swab for SARS-CoV-2 (antigenic or molecular test)
4. Onset of COVID-19 symptoms related ≤10 days
5. Clinical signs and symptoms of COVID-19 pneumonia
6. Imaging examination (X-ray/echo/TAC) of the chest compatible with COVID-19 pneumonia not requiring high oxygen flows
7. Low-flow respiratory support with Venturi mask or goggles with a pO2/FiO2 ratio (index derived from the ratio of PaO2 detected by blood gas analysis, to the fraction of oxygen, FiO2 administered) > 200mmHg
8. Body Weight ≥50 kg
9. Ability to provide informed consent
10. Ability to adhere to follow-up visits
Exclusion criteria:
1. Age <18 years
2. Seropositivity for HIV, HCV, HBV (HBsAg positivity)
3. Liver failure (Child A-C), renal failure (creatinine clearance < 50 ml/min), heart failure (NYHA IV), active stage neoplasms (those who have had cycles of chemotherapy including biologic drugs and/or radiation therapy in the past 6 months), ongoing neurological/psychiatric pathology (e.g., depression, psychotic crisis, suicide attempt)
4. Gastric/duodenal ulcer undergoing treatment
5. Systemic lupus erythematosus (autoimmune disease)
6. Hypersensitivity to cysteamine or penicillin
7. Drug/alcohol abuse
8. Inability to understand and sign informed consent
9. Presence of any physical or psychological condition that, in the opinion of the principal investigator, makes participation in the study not recommended
10. pO2/FiO2 ratio ≤ 200 mmHg
11. Need for oxygen at high flows (CPAP/NIV/VM/ECMO)
12. Use of antiretroviral drugs
13. Hemoglobin concentration less than 10 g/dl
14. Elevation of creatinine kinase at baseline more than three times the upper limit of normal
15. Abnormal laboratory values at baseline (baseline alanine aminotransferase (ALT) concentration more than three times the upper limit of normal, serum creatinine concentration more than twice the upper limit of normal, serum total bilirubin level more than twice the upper limit of normal, platelet count <100,000/mm3, white blood cell (WBC) <2500 (mcL)
16. Pregnancy or breastfeeding
17. Silico-tuberculosis
